life_budget.about: Box B (life design section 3, L1a): energy and nutrient caps per habitat. Production is the smaller of the energy cap and the nutrient cap (Liebig); biomass is production times a residence time; feeding levels follow from production density and a 10% transfer efficiency.

chemistry.label: carbon in water
sources: One example: Earth's life. Window, water activity and dose limits as box B's sources (window_k, min_water_activity, max_dose_msv_yr); recipe: Redfield 1958 (106 C : 16 N : 1 P); build cost as j_per_g_carbon
Bains, W. 2004, Astrobiology 4, 137: many chemistries could be used to build living systems. doi:10.1089/153110704323175124
Benner, S. A., Ricardo, A. and Carrigan, M. A. 2004, Current Opinion in Chemical Biology 8, 672: is there a common chemical model for life in the universe? doi:10.1016/j.cbpa.2004.10.003

metabolisms.label: aerobic chemolithotrophs (oxidising reduced compounds with oxygen)

sources.j_per_g_carbon: About 479 kJ per mole of CH2O for CO2 + H2O to CH2O + O2 (standard free energy of photosynthesis), 12 g C per mole
sources.window_k: Lower: about 253 K, the limit of cell division in brines (Clarke et al. 2013); upper: 395 K, Methanopyrus kandleri strain 116 (Takai et al. 2008)
sources.min_water_activity: 0.585, the lowest water activity known to support cell division: Aspergillus penicillioides (Stevenson et al. 2017, Environmental Microbiology 19, 687; https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/27871132/)
sources.max_dose_msv_yr: About 1000 Sv per year (around 0.1 Gy per hour), within what radiation-resistant microbes such as Deinococcus radiodurans grow under (Daly 2009)
sources.light_efficiency: 0.6% of 400 to 700 nm sunlight stored as fixed carbon, about the global mean that makes about 105 Gt C per year (Field et al. 1998); anoxygenic photosynthesis reaches 1100 nm (bacteriochlorophylls) but is limited by its electron donor
sources.c_per_donor: Stoichiometry: 4 Fe2+ per CO2 fixed (Widdel et al. 1993; Canfield et al. 2006); 2 H2 per CO2 (Kharecha et al. 2005); chemolithotroph and methanogen yields are order-of-magnitude growth yields (McCollom and Amend 2005)
sources.reuse: Ocean: each new phosphorus atom is reused about 1000 times before burial (marine P residence about 20 kyr against a turnover of weeks to decades; Benitez-Nelson 2000); land: about 46 times (Cleveland et al. 2013)
sources.c_per_p: Redfield ratio 106:1 in water (Redfield 1958); about 1000:1 in land plants and 186:1 in soils (Cleveland and Liptzin 2007)
sources.residence_yr: Marine phytoplankton turn over in days to weeks (about 6 Gt C standing against about 50 Gt C per year; Bar-On et al. 2018, Field et al. 1998); land plants about 10 years (450 Gt C against about 56 Gt C per year); deep subsurface cells turn over in centuries to millennia (Hoehler and Jorgensen 2013)
sources.transfer_efficiency: About 10% of production passes from one feeding level to the next (Lindeman 1942; Pauly and Christensen 1995)
sources.low_power_levels: Without oxygen, anaerobic metabolisms release about a tenth of the energy, so food chains stay short (Catling et al. 2005)

life_chemistry.about: Reaction energetics (evolution design sections 3 and 4, stage E0): standard free energies and enthalpies of formation of the species the life suite tracks, and reference reactions checked against published values. The gradient catalogue (E1) computes every reaction's energy from this table, moved to the local temperature and activities by the sse.chem blocks.

reactions.label: methanogenesis from hydrogen and carbon dioxide
nitrate reduced to nitrogen with hydrogen

sources.thauer: Thauer, R. K., Jungermann, K. and Decker, K. 1977, Bacteriological Reviews 41, 100: energy conservation in chemotrophic anaerobic bacteria; free energies of formation (appendix) and reaction free energies at pH 7. https://doi.org/10.1128/br.41.1.100-180.1977 (enthalpies of formation from the NBS tables, Wagman et al. 1982, J. Phys. Chem. Ref. Data 11, suppl. 2; values recalled, to verify: package log E0)
sources.convention: Elements in their standard state and the hydrogen ion at activity 1 have zero free energy and enthalpy of formation by convention
sources.bock: Bock, E. and Wagner, M. 2006, in The Prokaryotes, vol. 2, 457: oxidation of inorganic nitrogen compounds as an energy source (about -275 kJ per mol for ammonium to nitrite at pH 7). https://doi.org/10.1007/0-387-30742-7_16 (recalled, to verify)
sources.strous: Strous, M. et al. 1999, Nature 400, 446: missing lithotroph identified as new planctomycete (anammox, -357 kJ per mol). https://doi.org/10.1038/22749
sources.kelly: Kelly, D. P. 1999, Archives of Microbiology 171, 219: thermodynamic aspects of energy conservation by chemolithotrophic sulfur bacteria (about -798 kJ per mol for sulfide to sulfate). https://doi.org/10.1007/s002030050703 (recalled, to verify)
sources.stumm: Stumm, W. and Morgan, J. J. 1996, Aquatic Chemistry, 3rd ed., Wiley: Fe3+/Fe2+ standard potential +0.77 V, O2/H2O +1.23 V, so -44.2 kJ per mol at pH 0 (textbook)

life_history.about: Boxes C, D and E (life design sections 4 to 6, L1b): origin as a waiting time with a dial, innovations as a capability graph with waiting times against accumulated opportunity, and catastrophes from the physical chronicle with refuges and recovery. Defaults are tuned so Earth's inputs give an Earth-like outline in most seeds; that is one data point, not a law.

settings.label: land pools with wet-dry cycling and ultraviolet light
organics delivered by comets and meteorites

capabilities.label: chemical energy use
capabilities.effect: a base biosphere on chemical energy

capabilities.label: dormancy and spores
capabilities.effect: cells wait out bad times (survival of catastrophes and transfer between worlds come with L1c and L2)

capabilities.label: light harvesting without oxygen release
capabilities.effect: production rises 10 to 100 times where a donor is supplied

capabilities.label: oxygen-releasing photosynthesis
capabilities.effect: water becomes the donor, production rises again and oxygen is released

capabilities.label: complex cells (a merger of lineages)
capabilities.effect: cells with internal power plants: the hard step to larger life

capabilities.label: multicellularity
capabilities.effect: bodies of many cells; it arises often once complex cells exist

capabilities.label: large active bodies
capabilities.effect: animals that move, hunt and burrow: more feeding levels

capabilities.label: hard parts
capabilities.effect: shells and skeletons: fossils and reefs

capabilities.label: land colonisation
capabilities.effect: life on land under an ozone shield: land production joins the ocean's

sources.origin_rate_per_myr: The honest unknown. Set so an Earth-like early world most often has life within a few hundred million years (life by about 3.7 Gyr ago: Rosing 1999, Ohtomo et al. 2014); the origin dial runs from Rare (0.01) through Earth-like pace (1) to Common (100)
sources.settings: Alkaline vents (Russell and Martin 2004; Lane 2015), wet-dry pools (Damer and Deamer 2020), delivered organics (Chyba and Sagan 1992), mineral catalysts (Hazen and Sverjensky 2010); factors are relative weights, each switchable
sources.population_exponent: Innovation supply rises with population, but less than linearly (clonal interference; Lynch 2007); 0.25 keeps small biospheres able to innovate slowly
sources.activation_ev: 0.65 eV, the metabolic theory's activation energy for generation rate (Gillooly et al. 2001)
sources.rates: Waiting times in Earth-Myr of opportunity: anoxygenic photosynthesis soon after origin (by 3.4 Gyr ago, Tice and Lowe 2004); oxygenic within about a billion years (before 2.4 Gyr ago, Lyons et al. 2014); complex cells a hard step once oxygen exists (about 1.8 Gyr ago, Knoll 2014); large animals once oxygen nears modern levels (Ediacaran, Sperling et al. 2013); land colonisation needs an ozone shield (Kenrick et al. 2012)
sources.fragile_myr: New capabilities held by few lineages can be lost in a mass extinction (Jablonski 2001)
sources.recovery_myr: Recovery of diversity after mass extinctions takes about 10 Myr (Kirchner and Weil 2000); 90% at about 23 Myr
sources.oxidant_fact: Oxygen levels are inputs until L2 computes them from the balance; here they count only once a high-power (oxygen-making) metabolism exists

life_signatures.about: Box I: what observers can tell. Confidence is a posterior from the prior and the likelihood ratios of what is seen; floors are detection limits; gas amounts are sketches calibrated to Earth today.
sources: Meadows, V. S. et al. 2018, Astrobiology 18, 630: exoplanet biosignatures, false positives and context
Krissansen-Totton, J., Olson, S. and Catling, D. C. 2018, Science Advances 4, eaao5747: O2-CH4 disequilibrium
Luger, R. and Barnes, R. 2015, Astrobiology 15, 119: abiotic oxygen from water loss round M dwarfs
Seager, S., Turner, E. L., Schafer, J. and Ford, E. B. 2005, Astrobiology 5, 372: the vegetation red edge

Kiang, N. Y., Segura, A., Tinetti, G. et al. 2007, Astrobiology 7, 252 (Spectral signatures of photosynthesis II: coevolution with other stars), https://arxiv.org/abs/astro-ph/0701391: pigment absorption and the red edge shift with the host star
Reeburgh, W. S. 2007, Chem. Rev. 107, 486: about 0.5% of production decays as methane
Kasting, J. F. 2005, Precambrian Research 137, 119: Archean methane of 100 to 1000 ppm

life_sift.about: Box J: sifters name epochs by the newest capability and score them by persistence, reach, capacity change and reversibility (weights in that order); hooks raise stories. Defaults are in the code (SiftParams); a pack may override any field.

life_feedback.about: Box H: the stand-in physics side of the life-planet boundary. Life reports fluxes each step; this air box answers with O2, CH4 and a CO2 index. Oxygen builds only when organic burial and hydrogen escape outpace volcanic reducing gases and oxidative weathering, so oxygenation is a balance, never a date. Replaced by the planet layer's atmosphere and interior models when they exist.
sources: Oxygen as a balance of sources (organic burial, hydrogen escape) and sinks (reducing gases, oxidative weathering): Catling and Claire 2005, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.epsl.2005.06.013
Hydrogen escape and methane in the Archean irreversibly oxidise the Earth: Catling, Zahnle and McKay 2001, https://doi.org/10.1126/science.1061976

Falling reducing power of volcanic and hydrothermal gases sets the timing of the Great Oxidation (Holland 2002: gases slowly becoming more oxidised; Kump and Barley 2007: a shift from submarine to subaerial volcanism about 2.5 Ga). The e-folding decline here is a stand-in for both: Holland 2002, https://doi.org/10.1016/S0016-7037(02)00950-X; Kump and Barley 2007, https://doi.org/10.1038/nature06058
Bistable oxic and anoxic states through methane and ozone: Goldblatt, Lenton and Watson 2006, https://doi.org/10.1038/nature05169

Oxidative weathering rising with sqrt(O2) and the modern O2 budget: Holland 1978 (The Chemistry of the Atmosphere and Oceans, Wiley); Bolton, Berner and Petsch 2006, https://doi.org/10.2475/ajs.306.8.575
Land plants speed silicate weathering and draw CO2 down: Berner 1997, https://doi.org/10.1126/science.276.5312.544

Methane lifetime 9.1 +/- 0.9 yr today (total atmospheric; tropospheric OH alone 11.2 yr) and much longer in an anoxic air: Prather, Holmes and Hsu 2012, https://doi.org/10.1029/2012GL051440; Pavlov et al. 2000, https://doi.org/10.1029/1999JE001134

E3 competing sinks. Fire ignition index clamp(48 r - 9.08, 0, 5) and land-biomass factor k_fire / (k_fire - 1 + ignition) with k_fire 3: COPSE reloaded, Lenton, Daines and Mills 2018, Earth-Science Reviews 178, 1-28, eq. 4, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.earscirev.2017.12.004; photorespiration 1.5 - 0.5 O2/O2_0: COPSE, Bergman, Lenton and Watson 2004 eq. 4, https://doi.org/10.2475/ajs.304.5.397; Lenton and Watson 2000, https://doi.org/10.1029/1998GB900015 (checked at source 19 Nov 2026)
Fire does not spread below about 16% O2 and rises steeply from 19 to 22%: Belcher et al. 2010, https://doi.org/10.1038/ngeo923

Aerobic decomposition lowers organic burial efficiency as O2 rises: Betts and Holland 1991, Global and Planetary Change 5, 5-18, https://doi.org/10.1016/0921-8181(91)90123-E; COPSE reloaded uses it as f(O2) = 2.1276 exp(-0.755 O2/O2_0) (Lenton et al. 2018 eq. 35). The form and strength here are a stand-in, see docs/fudges.md
